requiredFutureAcceptance: Use one pinned custom PBX and pinned Python-only client; retain zero-exit network-free preflight, two-container internal networking, no published ports and all established isolation, resource, deadline, watchdog, warmed-inventory and owned-cleanup checks.
Register caller and agent using distinct ephemeral credentials; require exactly the two expected dynamic contacts and retain both endpoint/AOR configurations.
Add only PJSIP/proof-agent to the initially empty private queue and use timeoutpriority=app only in proof-queue.
Authenticated caller reaches private Answer -> Queue(proof-queue,r,,,3) -> Wait(10) -> Hangup. Host observes the caller Up in Queue and the agent Ringing before the agent is told to reply.
Agent sends 486 Busy Here for the correlated INVITE and requires matching non-2xx ACK; agent never answers and never establishes an agent BYE dialog.

Host observes only the original caller remaining in Queue with callerCount=1 after 486, then the original caller alone Up in Wait with callerCount=0, QUEUESTATUS=TIMEOUT, 3000 <= QUEUEWAIT_MS < 4000, ANSWEREDTIME_MS=0 and ABANDONED=TRUE.
Caller BYE returns 200 and drains all channels; require C:0/A:1, no completed agent calls, member removal and exact initial queue-policy restoration.

Both authenticated unregistrations return 200; require zero contacts/channels/callers/members, zero exits, unchanged warmed bridge/inventory and removal of all owned resources and generated credentials.
No retry, RTP/media-quality assertion, real phone interoperability, multi-PBX isolation, production use, Gate A/Gate C, deployment or redistribution authority.

offlineValidation.description: Packet-state, client, host, timeout, mutually exclusive mode and mocked orchestration tests only. No runtime credentials, real sockets, Docker resources or SIP traffic used.

limitations: The agent's 486 and matching ACK path is implemented in a bounded synthetic SIP client and is not a complete SIP conformance or real-device test.
The three-second application timeout includes host checkpoint overhead; failure to observe the required phases must remain a failure.
The queue path proves no agent answer and no completed queue call only if the runtime counters and member state match; mocks are not runtime evidence.
No caller-abandon/busy runtime attempt has been authorized or executed. Any runtime requires separate explicit approval.
No RTP, human service, tenant isolation, Gate A/Gate C, deployment or redistribution claim.
